subject: chemistry
subTopic: Crude Oil, Alkanes and Fractional Distillation

questions.content: Crude oil is pumped from beneath the seabed and sent to a refinery. What is crude oil?
options: A mixture of metals and carbon
questions.explanation: Crude oil is a mixture of hydrocarbons of many different chain lengths. It must be separated before it can be used.

questions.content: Which statement defines a hydrocarbon?
options: A compound containing carbon, hydrogen and oxygen
A compound containing only carbon and hydrogen
Any compound made by living things
questions.explanation: A hydrocarbon contains hydrogen and carbon atoms only.

questions.content: Alkanes have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. What is the molecular formula of the alkane with six carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: Using n = 6: 2n + 2 = 14, so the formula is C₆H₁₄.

questions.content: In an oil refinery, crude oil is separated into fractions in a tall column. What property of the hydrocarbons is used to separate them?
questions.explanation: Fractional distillation separates hydrocarbons according to their different boiling points.

questions.content: Which fraction leaves from the top of the fractionating column?
questions.explanation: The smallest molecules have the lowest boiling points and stay as gases until the cool top of the column.

questions.content: A student compares fractions from crude oil. As the hydrocarbon chain length increases, which trend is correct?
options: Boiling point rises and the liquid becomes more viscous
Boiling point falls and the liquid becomes runnier
Boiling point rises and the liquid becomes easier to ignite
Boiling point stays constant and viscosity rises
questions.explanation: Longer molecules have stronger forces between them, so they have higher boiling points and are thicker (more viscous). They are also harder to ignite.

questions.content: Which is the balanced equation for the complete combustion of methane?
questions.explanation: Each CH₄ needs two O₂: one carbon gives one CO₂ and four hydrogens give two H₂O. Oxygen atoms: 4 on each side.

questions.content: A faulty gas heater in a small room produces carbon monoxide. Why is this gas especially dangerous?
options: It is a very strong acid
It is colourless and odourless and stops blood carrying oxygen
It makes the room too hot
It dissolves in water to cause acid rain
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide forms in incomplete combustion. It binds to haemoglobin and cannot be detected by smell, which makes it so dangerous.

questions.content: A refinery uses cracking on long-chain hydrocarbons. What is the main purpose of cracking?
options: To break long, less useful molecules into shorter, more useful ones
questions.explanation: Cracking splits large hydrocarbons into smaller alkanes and alkenes, which are in higher demand as fuels and for making plastics.

questions.content: Alkanes are described as saturated. What does this mean?
options: They contain only single bonds between carbon atoms
They contain at least one double bond
questions.explanation: A saturated hydrocarbon has only single carbon-carbon bonds, so each carbon holds as many hydrogens as possible.

questions.content: Propane burns completely in air: C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O. The relative formula mass of propane is 44 and of carbon dioxide is 44. What mass of carbon dioxide forms when 4.4 g of propane burns completely?
questions.explanation: 4.4 g is 0.1 mol of propane. The equation gives 3 mol CO₂ per mol propane, so 0.3 mol is made, and 0.3 × 44 = 13.2 g.

questions.content: The fractions below are separated from crude oil. Petrol: molecules with 5 to 9 carbon atoms. Kerosene: 10 to 15 carbon atoms. Diesel: 16 to 20 carbon atoms. A molecule has 12 carbon atoms. In which fraction is it most likely to be found?
questions.explanation: 12 falls within the 10 to 15 range given for kerosene.

questions.content: A student says that the petrol fraction is a pure substance because it has been separated. Which response is correct?
options: Correct, because distillation always gives pure compounds
Incorrect, because each fraction is still a mixture of hydrocarbons with similar boiling points
Correct, because petrol has one boiling point
questions.explanation: Each fraction contains many hydrocarbons with similar chain lengths and a range of boiling points, so it is a simpler mixture, not a pure substance.

questions.content: An alkane has a relative molecular mass of 86 (C = 12, H = 1). What is its molecular formula?
questions.explanation: C₆H₁₄ has Mr = 6 × 12 + 14 = 86. C₆H₁₂ also has the wrong Mr (84) and is not an alkane.

questions.content: A refinery finds that the amount of long-chain hydrocarbons produced is much greater than the demand, while demand for petrol is higher than supply. Which course of action best addresses this?
options: Crack the long-chain fractions to make shorter molecules such as petrol
Burn the long-chain fractions without using the energy
Pump the long-chain fractions back underground
Dilute the long-chain fractions with water
questions.explanation: Cracking converts surplus large molecules into shorter ones that match demand. It is a standard refinery solution that avoids wasting resources.

questions.content: Which equation correctly shows incomplete combustion of methane producing carbon monoxide?
questions.explanation: Counting atoms in 2CH₄ + 3O₂ → 2CO + 4H₂O gives 2 C, 8 H and 6 O on each side. The third option is not balanced for hydrogen.

questions.content: Four students describe the fractionating column. Which description is correct?
options: It is hottest at the top, so small molecules condense there
It is hottest at the bottom, and long-chain molecules condense near the bottom while short-chain molecules rise higher
It is the same temperature throughout, and molecules are separated by size
It is coolest at the bottom, so bitumen leaves as a gas
questions.explanation: Crude oil is heated and enters near the bottom. The column cools with height. Large molecules with high boiling points condense low down; small ones rise and condense higher up or leave as gases.

questions.content: Decane (C₁₀H₂₂, relative formula mass 142) is cracked into octane (C₈H₁₈) and ethene (C₂H₄, relative formula mass 28). What mass of ethene forms when 710 g of decane is completely cracked in this way?
questions.explanation: 710 g ÷ 142 = 5 mol of decane. Each mole gives one mole of ethene, so 5 × 28 = 140 g. The equation C₁₀H₂₂ → C₈H₁₈ + C₂H₄ is balanced.

note:
## Crude oil and hydrocarbons
Crude oil is a thick, dark liquid formed over millions of years from the remains of tiny sea creatures. It is a **mixture** of many **hydrocarbons**, which are compounds containing only hydrogen and carbon atoms. Crude oil is a finite, non-renewable resource, and it is also an important feedstock for making plastics and medicines.

## Alkanes
The main hydrocarbons in crude oil are the **alkanes**. They are **saturated**, meaning they have only single bonds between carbon atoms. They form a **homologous series**, which is a family of compounds with the same general formula and similar chemical properties. The general formula is CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.
- Methane CH₄ (n = 1)
- Ethane C₂H₆ (n = 2)
- Propane C₃H₈ (n = 3)
- Butane C₄H₁₀ (n = 4)

To find a formula, put n into the formula: for six carbons, hydrogen = 2 × 6 + 2 = 14, so C₆H₁₄.

## Fractional distillation
Crude oil is heated until it vaporises and enters a tall **fractionating column** near the bottom. The column is hot at the bottom and cooler at the top. Molecules rise until they reach a height where the temperature is just below their boiling point, then they condense and are drawn off. Each **fraction** is a mixture of hydrocarbons with similar chain lengths.
- Top: refinery gases (LPG), then petrol, then kerosene, diesel.
- Bottom: fuel oil and bitumen, used for ships and for roads.

As chain length increases, the **boiling point rises**, the liquid becomes more **viscous** (thicker), and it becomes **harder to ignite**.

## Combustion
In plenty of oxygen, hydrocarbons burn completely to carbon dioxide and water, releasing energy: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O. In limited oxygen, **incomplete combustion** produces carbon monoxide and/or carbon (soot) as well as water. Carbon monoxide is toxic because it stops the blood carrying oxygen, and it is hard to detect because it is colourless and odourless.

Worked example: propane burns, C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O. The relative formula masses of propane and carbon dioxide are both 44. From 4.4 g of propane (0.1 mol) you get 0.3 mol of CO₂, which is 0.3 × 44 = 13.2 g.

## Cracking
Supply and demand do not match: crude oil gives more long-chain hydrocarbons than we need. **Cracking** breaks long alkanes into shorter alkanes and **alkenes** using heat with a catalyst (or steam at high temperature). For example, C₁₀H₂₂ → C₈H₁₈ + C₂H₄. Check that atoms balance on both sides. The alkenes made are the starting point for plastics.

## Environmental issues
Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas, and sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides, which cause acid rain. Oil spills damage marine life. Using less fossil fuel and developing alternative fuels helps reduce these problems.

## Common mistakes
- Saying that fractional distillation separates by "size" without linking this to boiling points.
- Saying fractions are pure. They are simpler mixtures.
- Forgetting that hydrocarbons burn to make water as well as carbon dioxide.
- Writing that cracking makes molecules bigger.

## How this is examined
Questions often set a refinery or fuel-supply context with a table of fractions, chain lengths and boiling points. You may need to read data, predict trends, balance combustion equations, calculate a mass of product, and evaluate the impact of burning fuels.

Exam tip: When explaining the column, always say that the temperature falls with height and link each fraction to its boiling point.

flashcards.back: A compound containing only hydrogen and carbon atoms.
CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. For example, n = 3 gives C₃H₈ (propane).
A saturated hydrocarbon has only single bonds between its carbon atoms.
Hydrocarbons are separated according to their boiling points as the vapour rises through a column that is cooler at the top.
Higher boiling point, more viscous (thicker), harder to ignite.

flashcards.front: Equation for complete combustion of methane
flashcards.back: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O
Carbon monoxide and/or soot (carbon), plus water. Carbon monoxide is toxic.
Breaking long-chain hydrocarbons into shorter alkanes and alkenes using heat and a catalyst.
Demand for short-chain fuels and alkenes is greater than the supply from crude oil, and surplus long chains are less useful.

subject: chemistry

questions.content: Alkenes are hydrocarbons that contain a particular feature. What is it?
questions.explanation: Alkenes have at least one C=C double bond, which makes them unsaturated.

questions.content: The general formula of the alkenes is CₙH₂ₙ. What is the formula of butene, which has four carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: With n = 4, hydrogens = 2n = 8, so the formula is C₄H₈.

questions.content: Bromine water is added to a gas and shaken. It changes from orange to colourless. What does this show?
questions.explanation: Bromine adds across the C=C double bond, so the orange colour disappears. Alkanes do not react with bromine water.

questions.content: What is the name of the alkene with the formula C₂H₄?
questions.explanation: The two-carbon alkene is ethene. Ethane (C₂H₆) is the alkane.

questions.content: What does unsaturated mean for a hydrocarbon?
options: It has at least one double bond, so it could add more atoms
questions.explanation: Unsaturated molecules have a C=C bond and could hold more hydrogens or other atoms if the double bond opens up.

questions.content: Ethene reacts with hydrogen gas in the presence of a nickel catalyst at about 150 °C. What is the product?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen adds across the double bond: C₂H₄ + H₂ → C₂H₆. The product is ethane, which is saturated.

questions.content: Ethene reacts with bromine. Which statement describes the reaction?
options: C₂H₄ + Br₂ → C₂H₄Br₂, an addition reaction
C₂H₄ + Br₂ → C₂H₂Br₂ + H₂, a substitution reaction
questions.explanation: The double bond opens and one bromine atom attaches to each carbon, giving a single product. This is an addition reaction.

questions.content: Ethanol can be made industrially from ethene and steam. Which set of conditions and name of reaction is correct?
options: Hydration, with a phosphoric acid catalyst at high temperature and pressure
Cracking, with a catalyst at room temperature
questions.explanation: Ethene plus steam is called hydration, an addition reaction: C₂H₄ + H₂O → C₂H₅OH, using a phosphoric acid catalyst at high temperature and pressure.

questions.content: Why are alkenes more reactive than alkanes?
options: They have a double bond that can open up to form new bonds
They have a lower boiling point
questions.explanation: The C=C double bond is a region where reactions can occur, whereas alkanes with only single bonds are largely unreactive.

questions.content: A student tests four samples with bromine water. Sample P: stays orange. Sample Q: turns colourless. Sample R: stays orange. Sample S: turns colourless. The samples are propane, propene, butane and butene (not in order). Which statement is supported by the results?
options: P and R could be propane and butane
P and R must be propene and butene
Q and S must be propane and butane
questions.explanation: Samples that decolourise bromine water are unsaturated alkenes, so Q and S are propene and butene. P and R do not react, so they are the alkanes propane and butane.

questions.content: Which of these is the correct molecular formula for pentene?
questions.explanation: Pentene is an alkene with n = 5. Hydrogens = 2n = 10, so C₅H₁₀. C₅H₁₂ is pentane.

questions.content: Ethene reacts with hydrogen chloride: C₂H₄ + HCl → C₂H₅Cl. The relative formula masses are ethene 28 and chloroethane 64.5. What mass of chloroethane can form from 14 g of ethene?
questions.explanation: 14 g is 0.5 mol of ethene. The reaction is 1 : 1, so 0.5 mol of chloroethane forms. 0.5 × 64.5 = 32.25 g.

questions.content: Why does an addition reaction have a high atom economy?
options: All the atoms of the reactants end up in the single product
It uses a lot of energy
questions.explanation: In addition, two molecules combine into one, so no atoms are wasted as by-products. The atom economy is 100%.

questions.content: A hydrocarbon has a relative molecular mass of 56 and decolourises bromine water. It contains only carbon and hydrogen (C = 12, H = 1). What is its molecular formula?
questions.explanation: A decolourising hydrocarbon is an alkene with formula CₙH₂ₙ, so Mr = 14n. 56 ÷ 14 = 4, giving C₄H₈. C₄H₁₀ has Mr 58 and is an alkane.

questions.content: Ethene burns completely: C₂H₄ + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 2H₂O. What volume of oxygen is needed to burn 5 dm³ of ethene gas, if all gas volumes are measured at the same temperature and pressure?
questions.explanation: Gas volumes are in the same ratio as the moles in the equation, which is 1 : 3. Five dm³ of ethene needs 3 × 5 = 15 dm³ of oxygen.

questions.content: A chemist reacts 14 g of ethene with excess hydrogen chloride and obtains 25.8 g of chloroethane. The theoretical yield is 32.25 g. What is the percentage yield?
questions.explanation: Percentage yield = actual ÷ theoretical × 100 = 25.8 ÷ 32.25 × 100 = 80%. Inverting the fraction would give an impossible value above 100%.

questions.content: A plastics company wants more ethene. Which statement gives the best justification for obtaining it by cracking?
options: Cracking turns surplus long-chain alkanes from crude oil into ethene and shorter alkanes, matching supply to demand
Cracking makes ethene from water and air
Cracking removes the need for crude oil
questions.explanation: Cracking uses large alkanes already available from crude oil and makes alkenes such as ethene. It still depends on crude oil, so it does not remove the need for it.

questions.content: A student wants to distinguish hexane from hexene without smelling them. Which procedure and result is best?
options: Shake each with bromine water; hexene turns it colourless, hexane does not
Burn each; the one that burns is hexene
Measure the colour of each; alkenes are always yellow
questions.explanation: Bromine water is the standard test for unsaturation. Both hydrocarbons burn and neither dissolves in water, so those tests cannot tell them apart.

note:
## Alkenes: the unsaturated hydrocarbons
**Alkenes** are hydrocarbons that contain a carbon-carbon **double bond** (C=C). They form a homologous series with the general formula CₙH₂ₙ. Because the molecule could hold more atoms if the double bond opened, alkenes are called **unsaturated**.
- Ethene C₂H₄ (n = 2)
- Propene C₃H₆ (n = 3)
- Butene C₄H₈ (n = 4)
- Pentene C₅H₁₀ (n = 5)

Note that there is no alkene with n = 1, because a double bond needs two carbon atoms. Alkenes are made from crude oil by cracking, and they are the starting point for plastics and many chemicals.

## Why are alkenes reactive?
The double bond is a reactive site. It can break open and each of the two carbon atoms can form a new single bond to another atom. This is an **addition reaction**: two reactants join to make one product. Because there is only one product, addition reactions have a 100% atom economy, which means no waste atoms.

## Key addition reactions of ethene
- **With hydrogen** (nickel catalyst, about 150 °C): C₂H₄ + H₂ → C₂H₆ (ethane). This is called hydrogenation and is used to make margarine from vegetable oils.
- **With bromine**: C₂H₄ + Br₂ → C₂H₄Br₂ (dibromoethane). Bromine water changes from orange to colourless.
- **With steam** (phosphoric acid catalyst, high temperature and pressure): C₂H₄ + H₂O → C₂H₅OH (ethanol). This is hydration.
- **With hydrogen chloride**: C₂H₄ + HCl → C₂H₅Cl (chloroethane).

## Test for unsaturation
Shake the substance with **bromine water**. If it is an alkene, the orange solution quickly turns **colourless**. An alkane leaves it orange. Be careful: say "colourless", not "clear", and not "decolourises" without saying the starting colour.

## Combustion
Alkenes burn too, often with a smokier flame than alkanes: C₂H₄ + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 2H₂O. Gas volumes follow the equation ratio, so 5 dm³ of ethene needs 15 dm³ of oxygen at the same temperature and pressure.

## Worked example
Ethene (Mr 28) reacts with HCl to make chloroethane (Mr 64.5). Starting with 14 g of ethene, that is 0.5 mol, so the theoretical yield is 0.5 × 64.5 = 32.25 g. If you collect 25.8 g, the percentage yield is 25.8 ÷ 32.25 × 100 = 80%. A yield below 100% is normal because of losses and incomplete reaction.

## Finding formulae
If a hydrocarbon decolourises bromine water, it is an alkene with Mr = 14n. If Mr = 56, then n = 4 and the formula is C₄H₈.

## Common mistakes
- Saying that alkenes are saturated.
- Using the alkane formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ for an alkene.
- Saying bromine water "goes clear" instead of orange to colourless.
- Treating addition as a reaction with two products.

## How this is examined
In exam-style tasks you might read about a chemical plant making ethanol or plastics from ethene, then be asked to state the type of reaction, write or complete an equation, calculate a mass or percentage yield, and justify why a method is chosen. You may also describe a test to tell an alkane from an alkene.

Exam tip: When describing the bromine water test, always give both the starting and the final colour (orange to colourless).

flashcards.front: What is the functional feature of an alkene?
flashcards.back: A carbon-carbon double bond, C=C.
CₙH₂ₙ. For example, propene is C₃H₆.
Shake with bromine water. Orange turns colourless for an alkene; an alkane stays orange.
A reaction in which two molecules join to form one product, with the double bond opening up.
C₂H₄ + H₂ → C₂H₆. Nickel catalyst at about 150 °C. Used to harden vegetable oils.
C₂H₄ + H₂O → C₂H₅OH. Steam, phosphoric acid catalyst, high temperature and pressure.

flashcards.back: All atoms in the reactants end up in the single product, so there is no waste by-product.

flashcards.back: C₂H₄ + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 2H₂O

subject: chemistry

questions.content: Alcohols form a homologous series. What functional group do all alcohols contain?
questions.explanation: Alcohols contain the hydroxyl group –OH. Carboxylic acids contain –COOH and alkenes contain C=C.

questions.content: Which is the correct molecular formula for ethanol?
questions.explanation: Ethanol has two carbons and one –OH group, so C₂H₅OH. CH₃OH is methanol.

questions.content: A brewer mixes sugar solution with yeast and keeps it warm without air. What is made?
questions.explanation: Yeast carries out fermentation, converting glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

questions.content: Vinegar tastes sour because it contains which compound?
questions.explanation: Vinegar is a dilute solution of ethanoic acid, a carboxylic acid.

questions.content: What is a polymer?
options: A very long molecule made of many small repeating units
A molecule with exactly two atoms
questions.explanation: Polymers are made by joining thousands of small molecules called monomers into long chains.

questions.content: Which is the balanced equation for fermentation of glucose?
questions.explanation: 6 carbons, 12 hydrogens and 6 oxygens on the left give 2 ethanol (4 C, 12 H, 2 O) and 2 CO₂ (2 C, 4 O). The second option balances.

questions.content: Which equation shows the complete combustion of ethanol?
questions.explanation: Counting atoms: left 2 C, 6 H, 7 O; right 2 C, 6 H, 4 + 3 = 7 O. The other equations are unbalanced or show incomplete combustion.

questions.content: A student adds sodium carbonate to ethanoic acid. What would they observe, and what is the gas?
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids react with carbonates, giving a salt, water and carbon dioxide. The gas turns limewater cloudy.

questions.content: A bottle of wine is left open and slowly turns sour like vinegar. What process explains this?
options: Ethanol is oxidised to ethanoic acid
questions.explanation: Microbes in air oxidise ethanol to ethanoic acid. Oxidation is the addition of oxygen.

questions.content: Poly(ethene) is made from ethene. What is the type of polymerisation, and why can ethene take part?
options: Addition polymerisation; ethene has a C=C double bond that opens
Addition polymerisation; ethene has a –COOH group
Cracking; ethene is a saturated molecule
questions.explanation: In addition polymerisation, the C=C bonds of many monomers open and join into a long chain with no other product.

questions.content: Ethanol and ethanoic acid are warmed together with a small amount of concentrated sulfuric acid. A sweet fruity smell is produced. What compound causes it?
questions.explanation: An alcohol and a carboxylic acid react to form an ester (here ethyl ethanoate) and water. Esters often have fruity smells.

questions.content: Complete fermentation of 180 g of glucose (Mr = 180) gives 2 mol of ethanol (Mr = 46), a theoretical mass of 92 g. A brewer collects 55.2 g of ethanol. What is the percentage yield?
questions.explanation: Percentage yield = 55.2 ÷ 92 × 100 = 60%. Inverting the fraction would give 167%, which is impossible for a yield.

questions.content: A town finds that plastic bags are lasting in landfill for decades. Which statement best explains why?
options: Most addition polymers are not biodegradable because microbes cannot break their strong bonds
Plastic bags are made of metal
questions.explanation: The long chains of addition polymers have strong carbon-carbon bonds that microorganisms cannot easily break, so they persist in the environment.

questions.content: Part of a polymer chain has the repeat unit –CH₂–CH(CH₃)–. Which monomer made it?
questions.explanation: The repeat unit has a two-carbon backbone with a CH₃ side group, so the monomer is CH₂=CH–CH₃, which is propene. The polymer is poly(propene).

questions.content: A molecule of poly(ethene) is made from 500 ethene monomers (C₂H₄, Mr = 28). What is the relative molecular mass of the polymer, assuming no other atoms are added?
questions.explanation: Addition polymerisation does not lose any atoms, so Mr = 500 × 28 = 14 000.

questions.content: A student argues that making ethanol by fermentation is more sustainable than making it from ethene and steam. Which is the best supporting argument?
options: Fermentation uses renewable plant sugars, whereas ethene comes from finite crude oil
Fermentation is faster and gives pure ethanol
Fermentation uses higher temperatures and pressures
Fermentation does not need any energy
questions.explanation: Sugar crops are renewable, but fermentation is slow and gives a dilute product needing distillation. Ethene hydration is faster and cleaner but relies on a finite resource.

questions.content: A technician has two unlabelled colourless liquids: ethanol and ethanoic acid. A small amount of sodium carbonate powder is added to a sample of each. Which result lets her identify them correctly?
options: The liquid that fizzes is ethanoic acid; the one with no reaction is ethanol
The liquid that fizzes is ethanol; the other is ethanoic acid
Both fizz equally, so they cannot be told apart
The liquid that turns blue is ethanol
questions.explanation: Only the carboxylic acid reacts with a carbonate to release carbon dioxide. Ethanol is neutral and does not react.

questions.content: An advert says: "Bioethanol is a carbon-neutral fuel because the crops absorbed carbon dioxide while growing." Which is the most balanced evaluation?
options: It reduces net emissions compared with petrol, but is not fully neutral because farming, transport and distillation use energy and land
It is completely carbon neutral with no environmental effects
It produces more carbon dioxide than petrol when burned
questions.explanation: The carbon dioxide released on burning was absorbed by the crop, which helps. However, fertiliser, machinery, transport, distillation and land-use change all add emissions and other impacts.

note:
## Alcohols
Alcohols are a homologous series with the functional group **–OH**. The first members are methanol CH₃OH, ethanol C₂H₅OH and propanol C₃H₇OH. Ethanol is the one you need to know best. It is used as a solvent, a fuel, and in alcoholic drinks.

Ethanol burns completely: C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O. Check the atoms: 2 C, 6 H and 7 O on each side.

## Making ethanol
- **Fermentation**: yeast turns sugar (glucose) into ethanol and carbon dioxide in the absence of air at about 30 to 40 °C. C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂. It uses renewable plant material, but it is slow, makes a dilute solution, and the ethanol has to be separated by distillation.
- **Hydration of ethene**: C₂H₄ + H₂O → C₂H₅OH with steam, a phosphoric acid catalyst, high temperature and pressure. It is fast and gives pure ethanol, but uses ethene from finite crude oil.

Worked example: 180 g of glucose (Mr 180) is 1 mol and gives 2 mol of ethanol, which is 2 × 46 = 92 g in theory. If only 55.2 g is collected, the percentage yield is 55.2 ÷ 92 × 100 = 60%.

## Carboxylic acids
Carboxylic acids have the functional group **–COOH**. Methanoic acid is HCOOH, and ethanoic acid is CH₃COOH, the acid in vinegar. They are **weak acids**: they only partially ionise in water, so their pH is higher than that of a strong acid of the same concentration. They show typical acid reactions, for example with a carbonate: acid + carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide, which fizzes.

Ethanol can be **oxidised** to ethanoic acid by oxidising agents or by microbes in air, which is why wine left open turns sour.

## Esters
An alcohol and a carboxylic acid react, with a little concentrated sulfuric acid as a catalyst, to form an **ester** and water. Ethanol + ethanoic acid → ethyl ethanoate + water. Esters often have sweet, fruity smells and are used in perfumes and flavourings.

## Polymers
A **polymer** is a very long molecule made from many small **monomers** joined together. In **addition polymerisation**, the C=C double bonds of many monomers open and join into a chain, and nothing else is produced. Ethene makes poly(ethene) and propene makes poly(propene). The repeat unit shows the original monomer with the double bond replaced by a single bond. For example, 500 ethene monomers give a polymer with Mr = 500 × 28 = 14 000.

Plastics are useful because they are light, strong, cheap and can be moulded. But addition polymers are not biodegradable, so they persist in landfill and in oceans. Solutions include reducing, reusing and recycling, and developing biodegradable plastics.

## Common mistakes
- Thinking carboxylic acids are strong acids because they have "acid" in the name.
- Confusing –OH (alcohols) with –COOH (acids).
- Writing that the polymer still has a double bond.
- Saying that fermentation needs oxygen.

## How this is examined
Questions typically provide a context such as a biofuel plant or a packaging company. You may be asked to identify functional groups, write equations, calculate a percentage yield, compare production methods, and evaluate environmental and economic impacts, for example by judging a claim that a fuel is carbon neutral.

Exam tip: When comparing two methods, give at least one advantage and one disadvantage for each, and refer to renewability, energy use and cost.

–COOH. Example: ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH, found in vinegar.
C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂ (yeast, about 30 to 40 °C, no oxygen).
Advantage: uses renewable sugar. Disadvantage: slow, makes a dilute ethanol solution that must be distilled.
C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O

flashcards.front: How are carboxylic acids classed as acids?
flashcards.back: They are weak acids, which only partially ionise. They react with carbonates to give a salt, water and carbon dioxide.

flashcards.front: What is an ester and how is it made?
flashcards.back: An alcohol reacts with a carboxylic acid, with a concentrated sulfuric acid catalyst, to make an ester and water. Esters smell fruity.
The C=C bonds of many monomers open and join into a long chain. No other product forms.

flashcards.front: Why are addition polymers an environmental problem?
flashcards.back: They are not biodegradable, so they last for decades in landfill and the oceans. Reduce, reuse and recycle.
